q: In the sitcom Friends, which premiered in 1994, what is the name of the coffee house where the group hangs out?
note: The six leads eventually negotiated their salaries as a single group rather than individually.

q: In The Simpsons, which began as a half-hour series in 1989, what is the name of the town where the family lives?
note: The show has never settled which state it is in, and the vagueness is the joke.

q: In the series Breaking Bad, which began in 2008, what subject did Walter White teach in high school?
note: He takes the alias Heisenberg, borrowed from the German physicist.

q: On Sesame Street, which first aired in 1969, which grouchy character lives in a trash can?
note: Caroll Spinney performed both Oscar and Big Bird for nearly fifty years.

q: The series M*A*S*H, which ran from 1972 to 1983, is set during which war?
note: The show lasted eleven years, more than three times as long as the war it depicted.

q: In the American version of The Office, which premiered in 2005, what is the name of the paper company where the staff work?
note: The branch sits in Scranton, Pennsylvania, and the series was adapted from Ricky Gervais's British original.

q: What is the rarely used first name of Kramer, the neighbor on the sitcom Seinfeld, which ran from 1989 to 1998?
note: The character was based on Kenny Kramer, a real-life neighbor of co-creator Larry David.

q: In the HBO series Game of Thrones, which premiered in 2011, what three words serve as the motto of House Stark?
note: The series was adapted from George R. R. Martin's novels, starting with A Game of Thrones.

q: What is the name of the starship commanded by Captain Kirk in the original Star Trek series, which debuted in 1966?
note: The original series was canceled after three seasons and only became a phenomenon in reruns.

q: In which American city is the bar in the sitcom Cheers, which ran from 1982 to 1993?
note: The exterior shots show a real pub then known as the Bull & Finch.

q: Which comedian starred as Lucy Ricardo in the 1950s sitcom I Love Lucy?
note: It was shot on film with three cameras before a live audience, which is why the reruns still look sharp.

q: What is the surname of the skeptical medical doctor partnered with Fox Mulder in The X-Files, which began in 1993?
note: Gillian Anderson was a near-unknown, and the network had to be talked into casting her.

q: Which actor played mob boss Tony Soprano in the HBO drama that began in 1999?
note: The series ends mid-scene with an abrupt cut to black that still divides viewers.

q: What was the nickname of Henry Winkler's leather-jacketed character on the 1970s sitcom Happy Days?
note: A 1977 episode in which he water-skis over a shark gave the world the phrase 'jumping the shark.'

q: In which city do the four housemates live in the sitcom The Golden Girls, which premiered in 1985?
note: All four leads won an Emmy for the series, a rare clean sweep.

q: What is the name of the dark parallel world in the series Stranger Things, which premiered in 2016?
note: The show is set in the fictional town of Hawkins, Indiana, during the 1980s.

q: The 1980 cliffhanger 'Who shot J.R.?' left the world guessing about a character on which prime-time soap opera?
note: The culprit turned out to be Kristin, his scheming sister-in-law.

q: Which writer created, hosted and narrated the anthology series The Twilight Zone, which debuted in 1959?
note: He wrote a large share of the episodes himself, often smuggling social commentary past the censors.

q: Which actor played the loud-mouthed bigot Archie Bunker on the 1970s sitcom All in the Family?
note: The series was adapted from the British sitcom Till Death Us Do Part.

q: What is the name of the New York advertising agency where Don Draper works in the early seasons of Mad Men, which premiered in 2007?
note: The firm is renamed several times across the series as partners arrive and depart.
